issues.failure_explanation: A usual nested base-b scramble bijectively permutes every finite digit prefix. In particular, it permutes prefixes of lengths e_j k_j, hence permutes the elementary intervals defining the mixed-base property and preserves their point counts. Coarse scrambling is therefore not necessary for preserving this structure. Its relevant distinction is the distribution of block permutations, especially two-fold uniformity at block level.

the variance is entirely contained in one-dimensional projections ($|u|=1$)

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis leaves lower-dimensional additive components uncontrolled. A counterexample, even with corrected definitions and fully nested uniform scrambling, is d=2 and f(x_1,x_2)=g(x_1), where g(0)=0 and g(x)=x^2 sin(x^{-4}) for x>0. The function is differentiable everywhere and its full mixed derivative is identically zero, hence Lipschitz. In a t=0 first-coordinate projection, around x proportional to n^{-1/5} there are order n^{4/5} strata with within-stratum variance of order n^{-4/5}; their estimator variance contribution is therefore Omega(n^{-2}), contradicting O(n^{-3} log n).

issues.failure_explanation: Comparing an exact variance with an upper bound for another method does not order their actual variances. There is an explicit opposite ordering even for a single-coordinate function: take a t=0 projection, n=2, coarse base 4, and f(x)=(-1)^{floor(4x)}. Usual binary scrambling has variance 1/2, while two-fold uniform base-4 scrambling samples two distinct quarter-cell signs and has variance 1/3. Thus low superposition dimension alone does not ensure usual scrambling is better; the within-coordinate frequency distribution matters.

failure_location.quote: For functions with a low superposition dimension, where low-order interactions (especially 1D projections) dominate, usual scrambling is superior due to its perfect $t=0$ property on 1D components.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Limit the conclusion to the tested integrands or impose an explicit low-frequency energy condition, and state that the formulas give no universal variance ordering for low-superposition functions.
issues.overall_effect: The paper overstates its theoretical and empirical comparison as a general preference for usual scrambling on low-superposition integrands.
issues.title: Low superposition dimension does not imply variance superiority of usual scrambling
issues.why_classification: A meaningful comparative guarantee must be weakened to a frequency-dependent or empirical statement, but the existing component formulas support such a contained replacement.
